source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֣י צִיּ֗וֹן גִּ֤ילוּ וְ/שִׂמְחוּ֙ בַּ/יהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵי/כֶ֔ם כִּֽי נָתַ֥ן לָ/כֶ֛ם אֶת הַ/מּוֹרֶ֖ה לִ/צְדָקָ֑ה וַ/יּ֣וֹרֶד לָ/כֶ֗ם גֶּ֛שֶׁם מוֹרֶ֥ה וּ/מַלְק֖וֹשׁ בָּ/רִאשֽׁוֹן־־׃
scope: Choose only timing wording under retained WLC consonants, pointing and segmentation; no first-gift, righteousness, tense or other wording change. Source historical priority separate.

candidates.K: And you, children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in Yahweh your God, for he has given you the early rain for righteousness; and he causes the rain to come down for you—the early rain and the latter rain at first.
candidates.M: And you, children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in Yahweh your God, for he has given you the early rain for righteousness; and he causes the rain to come down for you—the early rain and the latter rain in the first month.
candidates.R: And you, children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in Yahweh your God, for he has given you the early rain for righteousness; and he causes the rain to come down for you—the early rain and the latter rain as before.

source_context.source: אַל תִּֽירְאִ֖י אֲדָמָ֑ה גִּ֣ילִי וּ/שְׂמָ֔חִי כִּֽי הִגְדִּ֥יל יְהוָ֖ה לַ/עֲשֽׂוֹת־־׃
source_context.english: Do not fear, O land; rejoice and be glad, for Yahweh has done great things.

source_context.source: אַל תִּֽירְאוּ֙ בַּהֲמ֣וֹת שָׂדַ֔י כִּ֥י דָשְׁא֖וּ נְא֣וֹת מִדְבָּ֑ר כִּֽי עֵץ֙ נָשָׂ֣א פִרְי֔/וֹ תְּאֵנָ֥ה וָ/גֶ֖פֶן נָתְנ֥וּ חֵילָֽ/ם־־׃
source_context.english: Do not fear, beasts of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness have become green; for the tree bears its fruit, the fig tree and the vine have given their wealth.

source_context.source: וּ/בְנֵ֣י צִיּ֗וֹן גִּ֤ילוּ וְ/שִׂמְחוּ֙ בַּ/יהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵי/כֶ֔ם כִּֽי נָתַ֥ן לָ/כֶ֛ם אֶת הַ/מּוֹרֶ֖ה לִ/צְדָקָ֑ה וַ/יּ֣וֹרֶד לָ/כֶ֗ם גֶּ֛שֶׁם מוֹרֶ֥ה וּ/מַלְק֖וֹשׁ בָּ/רִאשֽׁוֹן־־׃
וּ/מָלְא֥וּ הַ/גֳּרָנ֖וֹת בָּ֑ר וְ/הֵשִׁ֥יקוּ הַ/יְקָבִ֖ים תִּיר֥וֹשׁ וְ/יִצְהָֽר׃
source_context.english: The threshing floors will be filled with grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.

source_context.source: וְ/שִׁלַּמְתִּ֤י לָ/כֶם֙ אֶת הַ/שָּׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר֙ אָכַ֣ל הָֽ/אַרְבֶּ֔ה הַ/יֶּ֖לֶק וְ/הֶ/חָסִ֣יל וְ/הַ/גָּזָ֑ם חֵילִ/י֙ הַ/גָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר שִׁלַּ֖חְתִּי בָּ/כֶֽם־׃
source_context.english: I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten—the hopper, the destroyer, and the cutter—my great army that I sent among you.

source_context.source: וַ/אֲכַלְתֶּ֤ם אָכוֹל֙ וְ/שָׂב֔וֹעַ וְ/הִלַּלְתֶּ֗ם אֶת שֵׁ֤ם יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵי/כֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֥ה עִמָּ/כֶ֖ם לְ/הַפְלִ֑יא וְ/לֹא יֵבֹ֥שׁוּ עַמִּ֖/י לְ/עוֹלָֽם־־־׃
source_context.english: You will surely eat and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of Yahweh your God, who has dealt wondrously with you; and my people will never again be put to shame.

source_context.source: וִ/ידַעְתֶּ֗ם כִּ֣י בְ/קֶ֤רֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אָ֔נִי וַ/אֲנִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵי/כֶ֖ם וְ/אֵ֣ין ע֑וֹד וְ/לֹא יֵבֹ֥שׁוּ עַמִּ֖/י לְ/עוֹלָֽם־׃ס
source_context.english: Then you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am Yahweh your God, and there is no other; and my people will never again be put to shame.

source_context.source: וְ/הָיָ֣ה אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֗ן אֶשְׁפּ֤וֹךְ אֶת רוּחִ/י֙ עַל כָּל בָּשָׂ֔ר וְ/נִבְּא֖וּ בְּנֵי/כֶ֣ם וּ/בְנֽוֹתֵי/כֶ֑ם זִקְנֵי/כֶם֙ חֲלֹמ֣וֹת יַחֲלֹמ֔וּ/ן בַּח֣וּרֵי/כֶ֔ם חֶזְיֹנ֖וֹת יִרְאֽוּ־־־־׃
source_context.english: And it will happen afterward that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.

evidence: Current local OT source query, not an independent manuscript count: seven other uses including defective spelling all occur with explicit day-of-month context. Joel lacks such a date formula. Pattern supports month ellipsis but does not prove poetic non-calendrical use impossible.

BDB target places retained form among first-month constructions, then recommends a different feminine Hebrew form for a former-state sense. Recommendation not attested letters and not straightforward formerly support under retained masculine form.

Keil retains masculine form and argues initial-stage meaning in contrast with subsequent Spirit promise, citing related but different forms in Gen33:2,Lev9:15,Num10:13. No exact formerly parallel is established.

Driver finds first-monthNisan plausible for latter rain but rhetorically unbalanced/redundant; treats initial-stage/former-state readings as requiring a different form. His argument conflicts with Keil, not an authoritative categorical prohibition.
Selected Greek and Syriac have former/before comparison; selected Vulgate has in principio without sicut. These do not uniquely establish a Hebrew exemplar or provide independent Hebrew votes.

Fletcher-Louis argues calendrical/cultic restoration, favors Tishri against reported TargumNisan, and interprets Greekfood without needed Hebrew amendment. This is a literary/cultic hypothesis, not proven calendar identity or actual bet/kaf exchange.
